startTimeout.description: How long the harness's session may take to become ready (its bootstrap and first session) before the attempt is an infra error, after one retry; default 90s.

DaytonaApiKey.description: The host variable holding a Daytona API key, made by `secret.fromEnv`.

DaytonaSandboxDescriptor.description: A Daytona sandbox per attempt, made by `daytona()` from `reeval/sandbox/daytona`.

apiKey.description: The host variable with the Daytona API key, read on the host only.

attemptsPerMachine.description: The attempts one machine runs at once, each as a user of its own, as `boat({ attemptsPerMachine })` does. Default 1.

dockerfile.description: A Dockerfile, absolute or relative to the directory of the file it's written in, that Daytona builds from its directory into a snapshot. `FROM ${REEVAL_BASE}` starts it from reeval's sandbox image; any other base must be Debian or Ubuntu based, and gets Node and the harness baked on top.

from.description: A Debian or Ubuntu based toolchain image in a registry Daytona can pull; reeval bakes Node and the harness on top into a Daytona snapshot, cached by content.

id.description: Cell id; defaults to `daytona`, or `daytona:<image>` for a recipe as for `docker()`, then `:<size>` with a `size`.

image.description: An image in a registry Daytona can pull, with the harness baked in and a `reeval` user, used as is.

install.description: Baked into the image in order, on `from` or reeval's sandbox image: no secrets, no workspace.

maxConcurrent.description: The most attempts on Daytona at once, across the run: machines times `attemptsPerMachine`.

prefix.description: The start of every sandbox name reeval gives Daytona, so a run's cleanup finds only its own: lowercase letters, digits and dashes.

reuse.description: A machine takes another of the run's attempts once one ends, instead of being deleted, as `boat({ reuse })` does. Default false, one attempt per slot.

DebugLine.description: One debug line: level 1 is `-v`, level 2 is `-vv` only.

detail.description: More lines under it, e.g. a docker command's output or a raw payload.

DockerSandboxDescriptor.description: A local Docker container, made by `docker()`, or a Podman one, made by `podman()`.

capabilities.description: Linux capabilities to add back, e.g. `['NET_RAW']`; every other one is dropped.

cpus.description: CPUs the container may use, fractions allowed. Default 2, capped at the Docker host's.

dockerfile.description: A Dockerfile, absolute or relative to the directory of the file it's written in, built from its directory with `REEVAL_BASE` set to reeval's sandbox image and cached by content hash.

engine.description: The container CLI the sandbox runs on: `podman` for `podman()`, Docker when unset.

from.description: A Debian or Ubuntu based toolchain image; reeval bakes Node and the harness on top, cached.

id.description: Cell id; defaults to `docker` (`podman`), or `docker:<image>` for other images, plus an install hash.

image.description: An image that already has the harness baked in, used as is.

install.description: Baked onto the sandbox image in one build container: in order, no secrets, no workspace.

maxConcurrent.description: The most Docker sandboxes at once, across the run, whatever their image.

pids.description: Processes and threads at once. Default 1024.

root.description: Run the agent, setup steps and checks as root, with the capabilities `apt-get` needs, instead of the unprivileged `reeval` user. For evals that install system packages at run time.

swap.description: Swap on top of `memory`, in the same units. Default: as much as `memory`; `0` makes `memory` the hard ceiling. A host without swap has none to give.

EgressPolicy.description: Where the sandbox may connect: any host over HTTP(S) through the egress gateway (`'proxy'`, the default), anywhere including raw TCP and UDP around the gateway (`'allow-all'`), nowhere (`'deny-all'`), or only the listed hosts (`'*.example.com'` matches subdomains). Under a restricted policy the harness's own hosts, brokered secrets' `hosts` and MCP servers' hosts are allowed too; any other request gets a refusal, and the attempt goes on.

EgressRecord.description: An attempt's network traffic. `allowed` is every host a restricted policy let through, its own and the automatic ones; null under `proxy` and `allow-all`. `recorded` is false when the sandbox can't see the traffic, and then `contacted`, `blocked` and `unresolved` are empty. Bytes are counted between the sandbox and the egress gateway, TLS included. `expectedBlocked` are refused hosts the harness always tries (its CLI's telemetry, say), kept out of `blocked`, so `blocked` contains only unexpected refusals. A request that carries the harness's brokered key off the endpoints reeval brokers it for is refused on a host the policy let through: it's in `blocked` once per method and path, its `reason` names them, and `connections` counts its requests. Past the first 20 pairs, the rest share one entry per host. With a setup policy of its own, every entry names the `phase` it happened in.

blocked.description: Hosts the policy refused, and requests that carry the harness's brokered key off the endpoints reeval brokers it for (one entry per method and path), each with why. A name that didn't resolve is in `unresolved` instead. A tunnel setup opened to a host the agent's policy refuses is closed as the agent phase starts, and is here with `closed: true`.

phase.description: With a setup policy of its own: the phase the connections were made in.

partial.description: True when traffic could leave around the gateway (`allow-all` in a container that kept its network): `contacted` lists only what went through the gateway, and anything that ignored the proxy (raw TCP and UDP, SSH, database drivers) went out unrecorded. Unset otherwise.

policy.description: The agent phase's policy: the harness's start, its turns and the checks.

setup.description: The setup phase's policy (files and setup steps) and the hosts it allowed, when it wasn't the agent's.

unresolved.description: Hosts the policy let through whose names didn't resolve (`metadata.google.internal` outside GCP, say), so the gateway answered 502 with the lookup's error. No policy refused them, so they're never in `blocked`. A record from an older reeval reads it as empty and has them in `blocked`, with a `can't resolve …` or `… has no addresses` reason.

EnvironmentRecord.description: An environment as it was applied, without secret values.

brokered.description: Secrets the sandbox only had placeholders for, swapped in by the egress gateway, named as in `secrets`. A variable it also got as its real value somewhere (an `http://` header, an env secret without `hosts`) isn't listed.

digest.description: Covers every field but the rules file's path; secret names are included; values never are. The image is the sandbox's.

egress.description: The policy the attempt's agent phase ran under (the harness's start, its turns and the checks), from the options and the environment; in the digest unless `proxy`.

mcp.description: The names of the MCP servers the agent was given.

overrides.description: Keys a later layer replaced, for example `env.KEY`, `skills.typescript`, `mcp.docs`, or `rules`.

parent.description: The previous `extendEnvironment` layer's name, else null.

plugins.description: The plugins placed, each with what it placed; in the digest. Unset when there are none.

secrets.description: Every secret, by the variable it's set as in the sandbox; an MCP header's (`secret.fromEnv`, `secret.template`, a plugin's `${VAR}`) by each host variable it reads.

setupEgress.description: The policy the setup phase (files and setup steps) ran under, when it wasn't the agent's; in the digest when set.

excluded.description: Paths left out of the sandbox by `exclude` (directories end in `/`); `.git` isn't listed.

plugin.description: The plugin the skill came with; unset for a skill from `skills`.

unset.description: Optional secrets whose host variable was unset, so they weren't injected.

workspace.description: This records the Git repository the workspace started as: the repo as written (a local one relative to the project root), the ref and path asked for (null when unset), the commit the ref resolved to, and the hash of the tree that was copied in, which is in the digest.

init.description: `init: true`: the workspace had a `.git` with one commit of the tree.

EvalCompareMeta.description: Which environment ran as the control, so the studio can show it.

from.description: Not written, since a compare names its control. A record that has it ran the eval's cascaded environment (`'environment'`) or an empty one named `baseline` (`'empty'`) as the control.

answers.description: The eval's pairwise questions (those with `across`), answered after its attempts by votes, one per question; unset without any. They annotate: `outcome` and `passRate` never depend on them. Each vote may include a short `reason` (capped). `reeval analyze` includes each answer in the digest (rates by cut, votes, ties, a failed call, and a sample of reasons). Each answer's `input` is the `<eval-slug>/questions/<n>.json` file: every call its model was sent, per pair and order, with secrets masked and screenshots as refs; unset where the evaluation's files weren't kept.

caseCount.description: With `cases`: how many the list has, `cases` holding those with attempts in this run.

cases.description: An eval with `cases`: each case that has attempts in this run, in list order, with its own cells. `cells` and `attempts` are over every case. Unset without cases.

compare.description: The baseline environment, when the evaluation uses `compare`.

excluded.description: The environments (and harnesses) `where` left out, one entry per case and environment, including those of a case it left out everywhere; unset when none.

family.description: In records from before an eval with `cases` was one entry, set on each case, which was an entry of its own. Never written now; reading such a record folds the cases into one entry.

fingerprint.description: Results are comparable only when fingerprints match.

id.description: `file › group › … › name`, as shown.

key.description: Used to match an evaluation across runs; equal to `id`.

lifts.description: With `cases` and `compare`: each variant cell against its control, paired by case. Its `minLift` gates the lift's lower bound, and a lift below it fails the variant cell.

outcome.description: Over gated cells, the outcome is `fail` if any failed, else `infra_error` if any is (a cell is `infra_error` only when nothing counted), else `skipped` if all were, else `pass`. An ungated cell's failures don't fail the evaluation. With `cases`, a cell's outcome is over every case.

passRate.description: pass@1, pass / (pass + fail), over the gated cells' attempts; infra errors and skips excluded.

revision.description: The eval's `revision`, part of the `sources` fingerprint part; unset when it sets none.

skip.description: Declared not to run: `evaluate.skip`, inside a `group.skip`, or left out by an `.only` in its file. Its outcome is `skipped`. Unset otherwise, so in a run that isn't `complete` a skipped eval with neither `todo` nor `skip` hasn't run yet. Unset on records from before it.

slug.description: Directory name inside the artifact directory, from `key`.

source.description: Hashes of what the `sources` fingerprint part covers but `revision`: the eval's body, its case data and its options with its groups'. Unset on records from before it.

sources.description: The evaluation file, by content hash: where the evaluation lives. Records from before `source` also list the local files it imported, and were fingerprinted over them.

todo.description: A placeholder, `evaluate.todo` or `group.todo`: it never runs, and its outcome is `skipped`.

verdict.description: In records from before an eval with `cases` was one entry, `family` on a case whose `gate: { passRate }` its family held over the mean of its cases. Never written now: see `CaseRecord.verdict`.

EvalMeta.description: Small summary carried through the engine's task metadata.

failedChecks.description: Each check that failed or couldn't answer, in call order, its message's first line.

score.description: The judge's probability that the answer is yes, from 0 to 1.

prepare.description: Its sandbox couldn't be prepared: reported once per sandbox, and it has no artifacts.

turnErrors.description: Each turn that ended in an error, as `turn 2 error: <message>`, so a failure shows why.

EvalPlan.description: How an eval was sized for the plan: what it asked for, and what a profile changed.

bestOf.description: Set by `runs: { bestOf }`: each cell stops once a majority of this many attempts agree.

brokered.description: Secrets any of its attempts brokers, as `NAME → host, host`.

capture.description: Resolved camera defaults when any field is set.

compare.description: Set when the eval compares variant cells.

egress.description: Each distinct egress policy its attempts run under, by environment and harness.

excluded.description: The case and environment pairs `where` left out of this case; unset when none.

familyExcluded.description: On a case of a pooled family, every pair `where` left out of any of its cases, so the record keeps a case it left out everywhere; unset when none.

gate.description: The eval's gate policy, or undefined when it was left at the default (`'all'`).

questions.description: The eval's questions, answered after its attempts; unset without any, or when a profile dropped them all.

runs.description: Attempts per cell; with `bestOf`, the most a cell runs.

sandboxWarnings.description: Its sandbox runs as root or with capabilities added back; empty for a skipped eval.

skip.description: Why the eval doesn't run at all, e.g. a profile's harness limit left none.

traitExcluded.description: The environments `--trait` or a profile's `limit.traits` left out; unset when none.

variants.description: Variants run, of those the eval compares; null without `compare`.

warnings.description: Warnings about the eval's setup, e.g. a moving git ref.

workspaces.description: Each distinct git workspace its attempts start from, as `repo#ref:path`.

EvalResult.description: One attempt's result. `id` is the eval's; `key` is unique per attempt.

attempt.description: Absent when the engine did not register an attempt for this result.

errorName.description: The first error's `name` (`TimeoutError`, `AbortError`), when the worker sent one.

formattedErrors.description: `errors` as Vitest prints them (diff, code frame), with ANSI color codes.

skip.description: Declared not to run: `.skip`, inside a `group.skip`, or left out by an `.only` in its file. Unset on an attempt a resume skips because it already completed.

todo.description: A placeholder (`evaluate.todo` or `group.todo`): no body; it's skipped and shown as todo.

EvalSource.description: An eval's own source as hashes: its body and case data as declared, and its options and its enclosing groups' in canonical form (`tags`, `revision` and `gate` aside).

body.description: sha256 of the body function's source text.

case.description: sha256 of the case's data as canonical JSON, with secrets in its strings masked as the record masks them; set on each case of an eval with `cases`.

ExcludedPair.description: A case and environment pair `where` left out.

harness.description: Set only when `where` read the harness.

ExecTry.description: One run of a `c.exec` command that had `retries`.

FailureClass.description: How a failure is classed. `config`: the user's setup is wrong (a bad token, a failing build step, a missing image) and fails the same way again. `transient`: the network, a 5xx or a quota, which may pass, so reeval retries it. `resource`: the provider ran out of memory or disk.

FakeHarnessDescriptor.description: A canned agent for tests and dry runs, made by `fakeHarness()` in `reeval/harness`.

bootstrap.description: A shell command the fake agent runs as its session starts, once per sandbox, as a real adapter's bootstrap installs its CLI: `tart()` bakes it into the image it clones, as it does a real harness's, so an attempt there finds it done.

brokers.description: In Docker, broker the key of the agent `layout` names (`OPENAI_API_KEY` for `codex`, Cursor's when unset) on that agent's endpoints, as its adapter does; OpenCode, Goose and pi take their model's provider's key, so with their layouts it's `FAKE_AGENT_API_KEY`, on no endpoint. The key stays on the host, and `exec` steps get a placeholder in its variable, which the egress gateway swaps in on those endpoints when sent as `Authorization: Bearer <placeholder>`, and refuses on any other request. For an agent whose bridge is a server in the sandbox (Claude Code, OpenCode, Goose, fx, Grok Build), it also serves on the session's first exposed port and reaches it from the host, as that adapter's start does.

costUsd.description: US dollars the fake agent says every turn cost, as a harness that reports its cost does; 0 reports none.

delayMs.description: Simulated turn length, honors the abort signal.

effort.description: Requested reasoning effort, recorded as `effort` on the cell. Use `servedModel` for what the turn reports (`fake-1[effort=medium]`). Fast is not this.

failWith.description: Throw before the first turn starts, to simulate an infra failure.

files.description: Files the fake agent writes into the sandbox on every turn.

flakeRate.description: Chance (0–1) that an attempt writes no files and says so, for flaky pass rates.

gateway.description: The gateway this harness's model calls go through, by name. It skips the config's `gateway` fallback: the plan refuses a gateway that isn't listed or can't serve this harness.

id.description: Cell id; defaults to `fake`.

ignoreAbort.description: Sits out `delayMs` even after an abort, like an agent that doesn't stop when it's told to.

layout.description: Behave like this agent: its image, and where it reads rules and skills (`CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/skills` for `claude-code`, `~/.gemini/config/skills` for `antigravity`, `~/.config/opencode/skills` for `opencode`, Goose's private home for `goose`, `~/.pi/agent/skills` for `pi`, `~/.agents/skills` for `codex`, fx's private home for `fx`, Grok's private home for `grok-build`). Defaults to the fake's own (`AGENTS.md`, `.agents/skills`) in Cursor's image.

maxConcurrent.description: The most attempts on this harness kind at once, across the run.

reasoning.description: A reasoning block at the start of every turn.

script.description: Real sandbox actions, one list per `c.send` (the last list repeats), run in order before `files`. `exec` runs as the agent: with the sandbox's own variables, none of the checks'.

servedModel.description: The model the fake agent says served each turn, as a real harness reports its resolved model and variant (`composer-2.5[fast=true]`); unset, it reports none.

startHangs.description: The first this many session starts of an attempt never become ready, even when aborted (`true`: every one).

startTimeout.description: How long the harness's session may take to become ready (its bootstrap and first session) before the attempt is an infra error, after one retry; default 90s.

text.description: The fake agent's final message on every turn; default `Done.`.

tools.description: Tool calls the fake agent reports on every turn, before writing files. `ok` defaults to true; null reports a call whose result never came. `durationMs` defaults to 0; null reports a call whose end the harness never said.

turnMs.description: Each turn's recorded agent time, exactly, whatever the wall clock says: a test can compare agent time without scheduling jitter, which four runs a side can tell apart.

usage.description: Tokens the fake agent reports for every turn, as `turn.usage`; without it, null.

withSkill.description: Files and message used instead when the environment gives the agent a skill.

FakeSandboxDescriptor.description: A temp directory on the host instead of a container, made by `fakeSandbox()`.

dir.description: Parent directory for the per-eval workspace (defaults to the OS temp dir).

id.description: Cell id; defaults to `fake`.

maxConcurrent.description: The most attempts on this sandbox kind at once, across the run.

FakeScriptStep.description: One action of a scripted fake agent. `exec` is reported as a `shell` tool call whose output is the command's stdout, `write` as file edits, and `reply` is the turn's final message. `mcp` (`'<server>/<tool>'`) starts the environment's stdio MCP server in the sandbox, as an agent would, and calls the tool with no arguments; it's reported as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. `error` ends the turn there with status `error` and that message, as a provider error would; one worded as a provider's credit, quota or rate limit makes the attempt an infra error. `refuseKey` ends it as the model API rejecting the key in that variable would, which makes the attempt an infra error.

FamilyEffort.description: The variant's effort against the control's, paired by case.

tokens.description: Over the cases where every counted attempt reported usage; omitted when none did.

FamilyEffortMetric.description: One effort metric over an eval's paired cases.

p.description: Wilcoxon signed-rank over the per-case differences; null when every difference is 0.

pairs.description: Cases with a value on both sides.

ratio.description: The median over cases of the variant's per-case median, over the control's; null at 0.

verdict.description: `insufficient` below 6 non-zero differences, where the exact test can't reach 0.05. `fewer` and `more` are the test's direction (which side's differences rank higher), not the median's.

FamilyInterval.description: A 95% interval on a pooled rate or difference.

method.description: `wilson` or `newcombe-paired`: one counted attempt a case and side, so each case is one Bernoulli trial (or pair). `t-cases`: several, so a t interval over the cases' pass@1, with attempts within a case never counted as independent.

FamilyLift.description: A variant cell against its control over an eval's cases, paired by case.

discordant.description: Set at one attempt a case and side: pairs where only one side passed.

minLift.description: The compare's `minLift`: with cases it gates this lower bound, not each case's.

p.description: McNemar's exact p (one attempt a case), else Wilcoxon signed-rank over the cases.

pairs.description: Cases with counted attempts on both sides.

variantRate.description: Mean pass@1 over the paired cases on each side.

FamilyMeta.description: A case's place in its eval with `cases`.

case.description: This case's index in the list, from 0.

cases.description: How many cases the list has.

id.description: `file › group › … › template`, like an eval id with the name template in place of the name.

FamilyRate.description: One cell's pass@1 over an eval's cases.

cases.description: Cases with at least one counted attempt in this cell.

cell.description: The cell's key, the same in every case.

outcome.description: Set with `passRate`: `fail` when `rate` is below it.

pass.description: Passes and counted attempts over those cases.

passRate.description: The cell's `gate: { passRate }`: with cases it gates `rate`, not each case's pass@1.

rate.description: The mean of the cases' pass@1; at one attempt a case, `pass / counted`.

FamilyRecord.description: In records from before an eval with `cases` was one entry: the eval over its cases, each case an entry of its own. Reading such a record folds it into the eval's `cases`, `lifts` and each cell's `rate`.

excluded.description: Every case and environment (and harness) pair `where` left out, including those of a case it left out everywhere, which has no evaluation; unset when none.

id.description: `file › group › … › template`.

outcome.description: `fail` when a lift is below its `minLift` or a rate below its `passRate`. A case still fails on its own under `gate: 'all'`.

ran.description: Cases with an attempt that ran (not skipped) in this run; fewer when a filter or tag left some out, or an interrupted run or a filtered resume hasn't run them yet.

FamilyVerdict.description: `lift` / `drop`: the interval excludes 0. `noise`: it doesn't. `insufficient`: fewer than 6 discordant pairs (one attempt a case) or 6 paired cases (several), where no test can decide.

FileRef.description: `path` is relative to the run's artifact directory; `sha256` is of the bytes on disk.

FingerprintParts.description: Each input of a cell fingerprint, hashed on its own, so a change can be named.

gate.description: The cell's gate (`none`, `passRate 0.5`); unset on the default `all`. Compare reads a change in it as a policy change, not a reason the runs can't be compared.

gateway.description: The gateway its model calls went through; unset on `direct`, each provider's own key.

harness.description: Over the harness descriptor, less concurrency caps.

image.description: The Docker image's id, or the digest of the image a `tart()` VM was cloned from.

judge.description: Over the judge's model, threshold and version.

sources.description: Over `EvalEntry.source` and `EvalEntry.revision`; on records from before them, over `EvalEntry.sources`.

FxHarnessDescriptor.description: fx through `@reeval/harness-fx` (`fx acp`), made by `fx()`. It runs on Vercel AI Gateway or OpenAI's API by the model id, or on OpenRouter or Vertex AI, and reports each turn's tokens.

effort.description: Reasoning effort, sent as `reasoning_effort` on each model call; only on `vertex()`, since fx sends none itself. Values are what the model takes there, e.g. `low`, `medium` or `high`.

gateway.description: The gateway this harness's model calls go through, by name. It skips the config's `gateway` fallback: the plan refuses a gateway that isn't listed or can't serve this harness.

id.description: Cell id; defaults to `fx:<model>`, or `fx:<model>[effort=<value>]` when `effort` is set.

maxConcurrent.description: The most fx attempts at once, across the run, e.g. for the key's rate limits.

model.description: A Vercel AI Gateway model id, `<provider>/<model>`, run on fx's `gateway` provider with `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`, e.g. `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`; or a bare OpenAI model id, run on OpenAI's Chat Completions API with `OPENAI_API_KEY`, e.g. `gpt-5.5`. On `openrouter()`, either runs on OpenRouter's Chat Completions API with `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, a bare id as `openai/<id>`. On `vertex()`, a Gemini model id, `google/<id>` or a bare `gemini-…` id, run on Vertex AI's Chat Completions endpoint, e.g. `google/gemini-3.8-flash`.

startTimeout.description: How long the harness's session may take to become ready (its bootstrap and first session) before the attempt is an infra error, after one retry; default 90s.

GatewayName.description: A gateway the config lists by name: `direct` is each provider's own key, as without `gateway`; `vercel` is Vercel AI Gateway; `openrouter` is OpenRouter; `vertex` is Google Cloud's Vertex AI.

diffHash.description: sha256 of the uncommitted changes (tracked and untracked, as a binary patch), when dirty.

dirty.description: Uncommitted changes, outside the `.reeval/` directory and the history folder, when the run started.

remote.description: The `origin` URL with any credentials removed.

sha.description: The commit the run executed at: HEAD when `reeval run` started. The later commit that adds the history file is a different, descendant commit.

worktreePatch.description: Those changes are stored as the `worktree.patch` file in the artifact directory. Applying it to `sha` reproduces the workspace.

worktreePatchNote.description: This explains why a dirty run has no `worktree.patch` file: it was too large, `artifacts` was `'none'`, or it looked like it held a secret (then where, and which rule, never the value).

GitWorkspace.description: A git repository (or one directory of it) the workspace starts as, from the `git` helper. `url` is what reeval fetches: the clone URL, or an absolute path for a local repository.

init.description: Give the workspace a `.git`: one commit of the fetched tree, with no remote.

path.description: A directory in the repository whose contents become the workspace.

ref.description: A branch, tag or commit SHA; unset is the remote's `HEAD`.

repo.description: As written: a URL, `github:owner/repo`, or a local path.

token.description: The host variable holding a token for the fetch; read on the host only.

url.description: What reeval fetches: the clone URL, or an absolute path for a local repository.

GooseHarnessDescriptor.description: Goose through `@reeval/harness-goose` (`goose acp`), made by `goose()`. It runs a model on its provider's key, and reads each turn's usage from Goose's `usage_ledger` (its ACP server counts one call).

gateway.description: The gateway this harness's model calls go through, by name. It skips the config's `gateway` fallback: the plan refuses a gateway that isn't listed or can't serve this harness.

id.description: Cell id; defaults to `goose:<model>`, or `goose:<model>[effort=<value>]` when `effort` is set.

maxConcurrent.description: The most Goose attempts at once, across the run, e.g. for the key's rate limits.

model.description: `<provider>/<model>`: Goose's `google`, `anthropic`, `openai` or `xai` provider on its own key, or the gateway's id on `vercel()` and `openrouter()`, e.g. `google/gemini-3.8-flash`.

startTimeout.description: How long the harness's session may take to become ready (its bootstrap and first session) before the attempt is an infra error, after one retry; default 90s.

GrokBuildHarnessDescriptor.description: xAI's Grok Build through `@reeval/harness-grok-build` (`grok agent stdio`), made by `grokBuild()`. It runs xAI models on an xAI API key and reports each turn's tokens.

effort.description: Reasoning effort as Grok's `default_reasoning_effort`, e.g. `low`, `medium` or `high`, for a model that takes one.

gateway.description: The gateway this harness's model calls go through, by name. It skips the config's `gateway` fallback: the plan refuses a gateway that isn't listed or can't serve this harness.

id.description: Cell id; defaults to `grok-build:<model>`, or `grok-build:<model>[effort=<value>]` when `effort` is set.

maxConcurrent.description: The most Grok Build attempts at once, across the run, e.g. for the key's rate limits.

model.description: An xAI model id Grok Build runs on the xAI API, e.g. `grok-4.6`.

startTimeout.description: How long the harness's session may take to become ready (its bootstrap and first session) before the attempt is an infra error, after one retry; default 90s.

HarnessDescriptor.description: The agent an attempt runs: a real harness, or the fake one.

HostedSandboxDescriptor.description: A VM per attempt from reeval's own VM service, made by `hosted()` from `reeval/internal/vm`.

attemptsPerMachine.description: The attempts one machine runs at once, each as a user of its own, as `boat({ attemptsPerMachine })` does. Default 1.

id.description: Cell id; defaults to `hosted`, or `hosted:<size>` with a `size`.

maxConcurrent.description: The most attempts on hosted VMs at once, across the run: machines times `attemptsPerMachine`.

reuse.description: A machine takes another of the run's attempts once one ends, instead of being deleted, as `boat({ reuse })` does. Default false, one attempt per slot.

InstallStep.description: A `docker({ install })` command, baked into a cached image layer: no secrets, root, cwd `/`.

JudgeArtifactRef.description: A capture this judge call sent as a file part. Bytes live in the `artifacts/<name>.png` file.

path.description: The `artifacts/<name>.png` path under the attempt directory.

JudgeRetry.description: One failed judge try that was retried, and the backoff before the next.

artifacts.description: Captures this call sent the judge as file parts, when any.

cost.description: `costUsd` as reported, else the call's tokens at the judge model's list price; unset when neither is known.

costUsd.description: What the gateway says the call cost, in US dollars (OpenRouter's `usage.cost`); unset when it names none.

gateway.description: The gateway from the config's `gateway` list the call went through; unset without one.

key.description: `<index>:<sha256(question) prefix>`: the same question at the same place in the evaluation, so a verdict can be followed across runs (and an edited question starts a new series). `<index>` is the call's place among the attempt's `c.judge()` calls, counting calls that failed, whichever finishes first.

resolvedModel.description: The model id the provider says served the call, when it reports one.

retries.description: Transient provider errors retried before this verdict, with the backoff before each retry.

upstream.description: The upstream provider the gateway says served the call (OpenRouter's); unset when it names none.

usage.description: The call's tokens; unset when the provider reported none, and for the fake judge.

Lift.description: A variant cell's pass@1 against the control's, on the same harness and sandbox.

control.description: Passes out of counted attempts (passes and fails) on each side.

interval.description: 95% interval on the difference, by Newcombe's hybrid score method from two Wilson intervals.

minLift.description: Set when the compare has a `minLift`; the cell fails when `interval.lo` is below it.

points.description: Variant pass@1 minus control pass@1, from -1 to 1.

withinNoise.description: The interval spans 0: the attempts can't tell the variant from the control.

LocalInput.description: One host file or directory a run reads.

path.description: Absolute; a directory for a `workspace`, a `marketplace` or a local git `skill` or `plugin` repository (a file for any other `skill` or `plugin`, and for an `npm` tarball).

symlinkTo.description: Set when `path` is a symlink in a skill or plugin: the absolute path it resolves to.

via.description: The symlink, inside a skill or plugin, it was reached through, when it's outside that folder.

LocalInputKind.description: What a host file is to the run: `eval` the eval file, `module` a file its load imported, `read` one it read, `tsconfig` a tsconfig.json it loaded under, `config` and `env-file` the config and its `.env` files, `lockfile` a lockfile reeval records, and the rest what the environment or sandbox names: `file` (`file()` and `directory()`), `rules`, `workspace` (a local `git()`), `skill`, `plugin`, `npm` (a local package spec), `marketplace` (a local one), `dockerfile`, `docker-context` and `plugin-build` (a local plugin's build context).

McpStartup.description: One start of a stdio MCP server during a turn (`turns[].mcpStartup`, in start order), timed by reeval's MCP timer, which every stdio server runs through. An agent CLI that starts one process per turn starts its servers on every turn; a CLI that keeps a session starts them on the first turn only. A server that doesn't answer within 60s fails the attempt as an infra error naming it; one whose client closes it first doesn't. `mcpStartup` is absent when the environment has no stdio MCP server, or the sandbox has no `node` to run the timer.

ms.description: Milliseconds from spawning the server to its answer to the client's `initialize`; null when it never answered (it exited first, timed out, or its client closed it first).

server.description: The server's name in the environment's `mcp`.

Observation.description: A `c.observe(name, value)` call: the last value given for the name.

turn.description: How many turns the attempt had sent when the value was given: 0 before the first.

value.description: Masked like the rest of the record.

OpenCodeHarnessDescriptor.description: OpenCode through `@reeval/harness-opencode` (`opencode acp`), made by `opencode()`. It runs on any provider whose key OpenCode sends in a header on known hosts, with that provider's key, and reports no usage (its ACP server counts one call).

effort.description: Reasoning effort for that provider: `options.reasoningEffort` (OpenAI) or `options.thinking` (Anthropic). Values are whatever that provider takes.

gateway.description: The gateway this harness's model calls go through, by name. It skips the config's `gateway` fallback: the plan refuses a gateway that isn't listed or can't serve this harness.

id.description: Cell id; defaults to `opencode:<model>`, or `opencode:<model>[effort=<value>]` when `effort` is set.

maxConcurrent.description: The most OpenCode attempts at once, across the run, e.g. for the key's rate limits.

model.description: OpenCode's model id, `<provider>/<model>`, e.g. `google/gemini-3.8-flash` or `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`; the provider picks the key.

startTimeout.description: How long the harness's session may take to become ready (its bootstrap and first session) before the attempt is an infra error, after one retry; default 90s.

PairFactor.description: A matrix factor a pairwise question varies; the others are held.

PairVote.description: One judgment of one pair of attempts, in one order.

a.description: The two sides by name: arms within a harness, harness ids across.

arm.description: Set on a cross-harness pair: the arm (environment) both harnesses ran.

artifacts.description: The captures each named side showed, by name; set when the question sends `artifacts`.

harness.description: Set on a within-harness pair: the harness both arms ran on.

reason.description: The model's short reason for this pick; omitted when it gave none. Capped.

run.description: The run number both attempts share, from 1.

swapped.description: True for the repeat that showed `b` first.

winner.description: `a`, `b` or `'tie'`, mapped back from the blinded labels.

PhaseTimings.description: The duration of each evaluation phase, in ms. `agentMs` is the harness turns; `diffMs` reading changes.

PiHarnessDescriptor.description: pi through `@reeval/harness-pi` (`pi --mode json` in the sandbox), made by `pi()`. It runs a model on its provider's key and reports each model call's tokens. It takes stdio and HTTP MCP servers, not SSE ones.

effort.description: Reasoning effort, passed as pi's `--thinking` (the CLI's name). Values are whatever that flag takes, e.g. `off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`.

gateway.description: The gateway this harness's model calls go through, by name. It skips the config's `gateway` fallback: the plan refuses a gateway that isn't listed or can't serve this harness.

id.description: Cell id; defaults to `pi:<model>`, or `pi:<model>[effort=<value>]` when `effort` is set.

maxConcurrent.description: The most pi attempts at once, across the run, e.g. for the key's rate limits.

model.description: `<provider>/<model>`: one of pi's providers whose key it sends in a header on a fixed host, or the gateway's id on `vercel()` and `openrouter()`, e.g. `google/gemini-3.8-flash`.

startTimeout.description: How long the harness's session may take to become ready (its bootstrap and first session) before the attempt is an infra error, after one retry; default 90s.

PlanEgress.description: One environment's egress on one harness, as the `--dry-run` table prints it.

policy.description: The policy as the plan prints it (`proxy` for the default), without the automatic hosts.

PlannedEgress.description: An attempt's egress: the agent phase's policy (the harness's start, its turns and the checks), and `setup`'s when the setup phase (files and setup steps) runs under another.

PlannedPhaseEgress.description: One phase's egress policy, and the hosts a restricted one allows on top of its own.

PlannedQuestion.description: A question as planned: its text, the model it names itself, if any, the factors it varies when it's pairwise, its choices, and the inputs it's shown of each attempt.

across.description: Set on a pairwise question; unset, it's asked of each attempt.

n.description: Its place in the eval's `questions`, from 1, kept when a profile drops one before it.

state.description: The inputs it turns on, besides `artifacts`.

PluginMarketplace.description: A Claude Code marketplace: the source that holds its `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`.

ref.description: A branch, tag or commit SHA; unset is the remote's `HEAD`.

PluginPart.description: A part of a plugin, as Claude Code's layout bundles it: `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, `agents/<name>.md`, `commands/<name>.md`, `hooks/hooks.json`, `.mcp.json` (or the manifest's `mcpServers`) or `rules/`.

PluginRecord.description: A plugin as an attempt placed it.

build.description: The tag of the image layer its build ran in (`reeval-plugin:…`); null without a build.

commit.description: The commit a git source resolved to (the marketplace's, for an entry inside it); null for a local or npm one.

marketplace.description: The marketplace it was listed in, with its `marketplace.json` name, its source as written (`github:acme/agent-plugins#v3`, `npm:@acme/plugins@2.0.0`) and the commit a git one resolved to (null for npm); null when the plugin was named directly.

parts.description: What it placed: skill, agent, command and MCP server names, hook events, and whether it had rules.

sha256.description: The hash of the files placed.

source.description: Where it came from, e.g. `local:plugins/review`, `github:acme/agent-plugins#v1:plugins/review` or `npm:@acme/review@1.2.0`; for a marketplace entry, the entry's own source.

PluginSource.description: A plugin to place for the agent, in Claude Code's layout, made by the `plugin` helper.

build.description: Commands that build the plugin in a Docker image layer, from its directory unless `cwd` says otherwise.

cwd.description: Where they run, relative to the source's root; default the plugin's directory.

run.description: The command, or the commands in order.

marketplace.description: Where the marketplace is: a git repository (at `ref`) or an npm package.

name.description: The plugin's entry in the marketplace's `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`.

only.description: The parts to place; default every part the plugin has.

build.description: Commands that build the plugin in a Docker image layer, from its directory unless `cwd` says otherwise.

cwd.description: Where they run, relative to the source's root; default the plugin's directory.

run.description: The command, or the commands in order.

only.description: The parts to place; default every part the plugin has.

build.description: Commands that build the plugin in a Docker image layer, from its directory unless `cwd` says otherwise.

cwd.description: Where they run, relative to the source's root; default the plugin's directory.

run.description: The command, or the commands in order.

only.description: The parts to place; default every part the plugin has.

path.description: The plugin's directory in the package; default its root.

build.description: Commands that build the plugin in a Docker image layer, from its directory unless `cwd` says otherwise.

cwd.description: Where they run, relative to the source's root; default the plugin's directory.

run.description: The command, or the commands in order.

only.description: The parts to place; default every part the plugin has.

path.description: The plugin's directory in the repository; default its root.

ref.description: A branch, tag or commit SHA; unset is the remote's `HEAD`.

repo.description: As written: a URL, `github:owner/repo`, or a GitHub `/tree/<ref>/<path>` URL.

PrepareFailure.description: What failed, as the record, the terminal and `summary.md` report it.

cause.description: A resource failure's cause, named in the headline.

log.description: The provider's full output for the step, when it wrote one.

message.description: The headline first, then the step's last lines.

ref.description: What was being made, e.g. an image tag; null when there's nothing to name.

setBy.description: The levels that set the sandbox, once reeval knows them.

stage.description: The provider's name for the step that failed, e.g. `install` or `dockerfile` for Docker.

usage.description: Fixing it means changing the config or the environment (exit 2), not rerunning (exit 3).

PrepareFailureRecord.description: The sandbox an attempt needed that couldn't be prepared before the run, on each attempt that needed it: its provider's stage (Docker's `image`, `from`, `dockerfile`, `harness` or `install`, or `workspace` for a git workspace, whose `ref` is `repo#ref:path`), what was being made, the class (`config`, `transient` after the retries, or `resource`), a named cause (`enospc`, `oom`), the build log, and the levels that set it.

PrepareTargetView.description: A sandbox preflight prepares, as the terminal names it.

kind.description: The provider: the sandbox's kind, or `podman` for a Docker sandbox on Podman.

label.description: How the terminal names it, e.g. `docker:python`.

runWide.description: Set by the config or a profile, sandbox and harness both: a failure stops the run.

setBy.description: The levels that set the sandbox, or the environments its plugin builds come from, in first-use order.

Progress.description: A progress update stamped with the worker's clock (epoch ms).

try.description: With `retries`: the try it ended on, of `tries` it could make.

error.description: The turn's first error event, e.g. the provider's billing or auth error.

filesChanged.description: The files the turn changed, from the workspace diff, so a file the shell wrote counts. Unset when the turn didn't get as far as a diff.

ProviderStopRecord.description: The model provider ended a turn, not the agent: out of credit, over its quota, rate limited or overloaded, with the HTTP status of the last model call the egress gateway brokered when that call failed (`null` when it didn't, as in a stream that failed inside an HTTP 200, or none was). The attempt is then an infra error, so `--retry-errors` runs it again.

QuestionStateOptions.description: A planned question's inputs but `artifacts`, and `turns`: what `compare` resolves.

checks.description: `c.exec` results; a list shows only those commands, as passed to `c.exec`.

diff.description: The diff since the eval started. A list is gitignore-style patterns over workspace paths: the last matching pattern wins and `!` excludes.

files.description: `status path` lines for the changed files, under `diff`'s patterns.

observations.description: `c.observe()` values, by name; a list shows only those names.

output.description: The final message: the agent's own account of its work.

task.description: The prompts the attempt was sent, once for both sides when they match.

transcript.description: The transcript as text lines: `true` is messages and tool calls with tool output clipped, `'tools'` tool calls only, `'full'` adds reasoning and whole tool output. It names each harness's tools, so a pair of two harnesses isn't blind.

turns.description: `'all'`: every turn under `turns`, each with its task, output and (with `transcript`) transcript; `'last'`: the last turn only. Default `'all'`.

Remark.description: A remark about the eval's quality, not about the agent.

brief.description: The remark as one short line, with its fix and where (`1 run per side; set runs: 4 at evals/a.eval.ts:12 to confirm these differences.`), which `reeval run`'s list prints without `-v`; absent when the kind has none.

evidence.description: Facts from this run (or history facts) showing it mattered now.

firstSeenRun.description: The first run that printed this `id`, or this run when none has: it prints only in that run, except the kinds about the environment, which print in every run they happen.

fix.description: An edit at a source location (`source:<file>#L<n>`) in the eval.

id.description: sha256(kind, evalId, the eval's sources hash, and for `slow-mcp-start` the server): one remark per kind (and server) per eval version.

printed.description: Whether this run's `reeval run` output printed it: false when an earlier run printed it, or when the cap or a run without `-v` left it out, so a later run prints it.

ResolvedGateway.description: Where a cell's harness resolved in the `gateway` list, and the entries before it that couldn't serve it.

ResolvedJudgeStateOptions.description: The inputs one judge call saw, every key set (`false` when off); `artifacts` is recorded apart.

observations.description: Set only when the call turned it on, so never `false` as written.

ResolvedQuestionStateOptions.description: `QuestionStateOptions` with every key set: what each side of one question showed.

observations.description: Set only when the question turned it on, so never `false` as written.

ResourceFailureRecord.description: The sandbox ran out of a resource during the attempt: `oom` is the kernel killing `kills` processes at its memory limit. The attempt is then an infra error, whatever its checks said.

dropped.description: Files left out because the secret scan found something in them, with what it found.

RunEventLine.description: One line of a run's event stream.

concurrency.description: How many attempts run at once.

details.description: `--dry-run`'s table, image status and cost lines.

notRun.description: Attempts the run planned that this resume's filters left out and that aren't done.

remarks.description: The run's remarks, or null when it raised none.

results.description: The engine's results, for Vitest-formatted failure details.

summaryPath.description: summary.md, or the record itself when there are no artifacts.

RunEventsExit.description: The last line a `reeval run` writes to the stream: its exit code.

RunEventsHeader.description: The first line a `reeval run` writes to the stream: what the renderers need to draw it.

cwd.description: The `reeval run`'s current directory from its project root, as a `/` path (`''` when it ran in the root). The paths the run prints are from that directory, so a reader turns them into the project's with it. Absent from an older reeval's streams, and when the two share no path.

harness.description: The config's first harness kind, which names attempts' axes on detail lines.

heartbeatMs.description: How often a quiet stream gets a heartbeat line, so a reader can treat silence as a stall from the header on. Absent from streams that write none, such as an older reeval's.

pid.description: The `reeval run` process and its host, so a reader can tell a run that died.

reeval.description: The reeval that wrote the stream.

startedAt.description: When this `reeval run` (the run, or a resume of it) started, as ISO 8601.

verbosity.description: `-v` (1) or `-vv` (2): how debug lines' times read; 0 without either.

RunEventsHeartbeat.description: Written while the stream is otherwise quiet, so a reader can tell a run that's still going from one that stalled or was lost. Streams from before it have none.

RunHeader.description: What the plan line says, as the facts a terminal's run header lists one per line.

attempts.description: The most attempts the plan may start, and the fewest it starts (below with best-of).

config.description: The config file, when it isn't in the current directory.

efforts.description: The effort each harness runs at, by id (its level, `none` or `not checked`); unset with only the fake harness.

estimateMs.description: Serial: every attempt one after another.

judges.description: The judge models the planned attempts use.

parallel.description: How many attempts run at once, below `concurrency` when a sandbox provider caps it.

record.description: Where the run's record lands; unset for `--dry-run`.

resumed.description: Attempts already completed in the run this one resumes.

retried.description: Attempts it runs again after an infra error.

RunInvocation.description: The `reeval run` settings that shaped a run's plan, as it was first started. A resume keeps them, so it finishes the attempts the run planned.

concurrency.description: `--concurrency` or `REEVAL_CONCURRENCY`; unset when the config or the machine sized it.

events.description: The file `--events` wrote the run's event stream to, from the project root in posix form (`../…` outside it), so a resume appends to it; unset without `--events`.

profile.description: The profile the run was sized with; unset when it had none.

runs.description: `--runs`; unset when each cell ran its own `runs`.

pr.description: The pull request a CI run built, when the provider says (GitHub Actions).

artifacts.description: Which artifacts sit next to this record. Refs to files that weren't kept are removed.

config.description: The run's settings. `sandbox` is the id of each sandbox the planned attempts ran on, after the profile's defaults, joined with `, `.

concurrency.description: Attempts that ran at once; not part of `configHash`, since it doesn't change results.

runs.description: The config's `runs` (with `bestOf`, the most a cell runs); 1 when it sets none, though a compare's cells then run 4 each.

debug.description: The attempts' debug data uploaded with the run to its store (`history.debug`), each file by its path in `.reeval/debug/<run>/` (`<eval>/<cell>/<n>/requests.ndjson`); absent when none was.

lockfiles.description: Lockfiles in the project root (and the repo root, if different), by content hash.

durationMs.description: How long the run ran, counting each `--retry-errors` of it but not the time between them.

environments.description: Each environment the run applied, fingerprinted; secret values are never included.

errors.description: These are redacted errors outside any attempt: an evaluation file that didn't load, a rejection or throw no attempt awaited, or a worker that died. Any one fails the run. Unset when there were none.

families.description: In records from before an eval with `cases` was one entry, each eval with `cases` that ran. Never written now; reading such a record folds it into its eval.

invocation.description: How `reeval run` was started; `--resume` plans with it again. Unset in older records.

plan.description: What the run planned before it started, and each level whose sandbox ran as root or with capabilities added back.

profile.description: The profile the run was sized with, and why it was chosen.

runs.description: With `bestOf`, the most attempts a cell runs.

retriedAt.description: When each `reeval run --retry-errors` of the run started, oldest first; unset for a run never retried. A `--resume` of the run while it's `interrupted` finishes the last one.

runId.description: Also the file name: `<UTC start>_<short sha>_<author or ci>`.

status.description: `budget` when `budget.duration` stopped new attempts from starting.

RunRemarks.description: A run's remarks, `<history>/<run>/remarks.json`. Written only when the run raised one.

remarks.description: Every remark this run raised, ranked, including those an earlier run printed first (`firstSeenRun`), which don't print again.

notGated.description: Failed attempts in ungated cells (controls, by default), which don't fail the run.

SandboxBase.description: The saved image a VM sandbox's attempt ran in: the provider's snapshot its VM started from, and the image in it that the attempt's container ran, built from the sandbox's image recipe.

built.description: This run built the snapshot, rather than finding it saved.

image.description: The image in the snapshot the attempt's container ran.

key.description: The recipe's content key, which names both.

pinned.description: False when a base image couldn't be resolved to a digest, so the key names its tag.

SandboxWarning.description: A `SandboxWarning` describes a sandbox with more privilege than the default `reeval` user: `docker({ root: true })` or `docker({ capabilities })`. One per level that set such a sandbox, however many evaluations inherit it.

file.description: The evaluation file that sets it, for a group or evaluation; null for the config or a profile.

message.description: The line reeval prints after `⚠  Warning:`, in red for root and orange for capabilities.

where.description: The value is the level as reeval names it: the `reeval.config.ts` file, `profiles.pr.defaults`, `group("net")`, or `evaluate("installs deps")`.

address.description: The address it listens on there, e.g. `127.0.0.1`, `::1` or `0.0.0.0`; empty when the sandbox can't tell.

command.description: The command as the eval passed it.

detected.description: It listened on a port other than `PORT`, the one that started listening after it did.

port.description: The port it listens on, which the handle and `c.capture` use.

portEnv.description: The `PORT` it was given: the port the eval passed, or the one reeval allocated.

readyMs.description: From the command's start until it listened.

SetupProcess.description: A process the setup steps left running in a Docker sandbox with a `to: 'checks'` secret without `hosts` in its environment: it holds the real value while the agent works.

command.description: Its command line, cut at 200 characters.

secrets.description: The `to: 'checks'` secrets without `hosts` in its environment, by name.

SkillPlacement.description: `harness` (default): the agent's own skills, via its adapter. `workspace`: its repo skill dir.

Snapshot.description: A copy of the attempt's workspace, taken in the sandbox (never recorded into the history folder), or why it wasn't.

bytes.description: Its size on disk: the directory's files, or the tarball; 0 when it wasn't taken.

dropped.description: Binary files left out because they held a secret-looking value, at most 50.

excluded.description: Directories left out by name, such as `node_modules/` and `.git/`, at most 50.

files.description: Regular files and symbolic links in it.

form.description: A plain directory, or a gzipped tarball with `snapshot: { compress: true }`.

masked.description: Text files whose secret-looking values were masked, at most 50.

name.description: `final` after the checks, or `turn-<n>` after the nth `c.send`.

path.description: Where it is, relative to the run's directory in `.reeval/runs`: `<eval>/<cell>/<n>/snapshots/<name>` (with `.tar.gz` when compressed); null when it wasn't taken.

skipped.description: Why it wasn't taken: `size` when the workspace was over its form's cap, `error` when the sandbox couldn't archive it; null when it was.

Stack.description: These fields describe what ran and graded the agents: the machine, images, harnesses, and judge.

context.description: Union of every attempt's context files.

fingerprintScope.description: What evaluation fingerprints hash; fingerprints from different scopes aren't comparable.

harnesses.description: For each harness, the record includes its configured `model` and the `effort` it ran at, `resolvedModels` (what it reported serving, with the variant it resolved), and `resolvedEffort` (reasoning-effort suffixes those labels named). Fast (`[fast=true]`) is not `resolvedEffort`.

effort.description: The reasoning effort reeval asked the harness for: the factory's, or `medium` where it set none and the harness and model take one; null when reeval asked for none, leaving the CLI's own default. Fast is not this.

model.description: The configured model, when the harness has one.

resolvedEffort.description: Reasoning-effort suffixes those served models named (`medium` from `gpt-5.6-luna[effort=medium]`); empty when they name none. Fast is not this.

resolvedModels.description: The models the harness reported serving, across every turn in the run, with the variant it resolved (`composer-2.5[fast=false]` for `composer-2.5` with no `params`); empty when it reports none.

images.description: Every image an attempt started from. `id` is content-addressed; `repoDigests` exist only after the image is pushed.

base.description: The harness image the `install` layers were baked onto: `ref` itself without any.

dockerfile.description: `docker({ dockerfile })`: the path from the project root and the build context's hash.

from.description: `docker({ from })`: the base as written and the digest the image was built on (a local-only base's image id); `reeval image build` rebuilds it when the tag has moved since.

id.description: Content-addressed image id (`sha256:…`).

judge.description: The run's judge: the config's, with what the profile's `judge` and `defaults.judge` set over it. `config.judgeModel` and `config.threshold` name the same one.

model.description: Its model; groups, evals and calls may use others (see each verdict).

resolvedModels.description: Model ids the provider reported serving, across every judge call in the run.

state.description: The config's default judge inputs, every key resolved. Unset when the config names none, which reeval requires: each `c.judge()` call names its own.

version.description: Changes when reeval, the AI SDK or the provider adapter (and so the judge prompt) change.

language.description: The evaluation language, `typescript` for `*.eval.ts` files, and the version of its toolchain when the runner reports one.

node.description: `process.versions.node`, or the compatible Node version reported by another runtime.

packages.description: Exact versions of the packages that run and grade the agent.

reeval.description: The reeval version that wrote the run.

runtime.description: The runtime reeval ran on, `node`, `bun`, `deno`, or another, and its version.

StartRetry.description: A harness session start that timed out, or failed on a transient error, and was started again.

error.description: `<harness kind>: session did not become ready within <startTimeout>`, or the transient error the start failed on, such as `Cursor harness failed to start: Cursor's model catalog request failed: HTTP 502 (tried 3 times)`.

waitedMs.description: How long it waited before giving up on that start, or until that start failed.

TartHost.description: A Mac that runs `tart()`'s VMs over SSH: an SSH destination, or its parts.

host.description: The host name, address or `~/.ssh/config` alias.

identityFile.description: The private key `ssh -i` takes: absolute, or `~/…`; the agent's or the config's when unset.

port.description: The SSH port; `ssh`'s own (the config's, or 22) when unset.

user.description: The login user; `ssh`'s own (the config's, or this machine's user) when unset.

vms.description: The most of reeval's macOS VMs it runs at once: 1 or 2, and 2 when unset.

TartSandboxDescriptor.description: A macOS VM on this Mac, cloned from `image` for each attempt by Tart, made by `tart()`.

cpus.description: CPUs each clone gets; the image's when unset.

hosts.description: Macs that run the VMs instead of this machine, each one plain `ssh` reaches without a prompt (an `~/.ssh/config` alias, the agent or a key file; no passwords): `'mac-studio'`, `'elliot@mac-mini.local'`, `'ssh://ci@10.0.0.5:2222'` or `{ host, user?, port?, identityFile?, vms? }`. reeval runs `tart` on each over SSH and keeps the egress gateway, and every key, here. Each host needs the image; preflight bakes the harness onto it there. This machine when unset.

id.description: Cell id; defaults to `tart:<image>`, the image's last path segment.

image.description: The VM each attempt clones: an OCI image such as `ghcr.io/cirruslabs/macos-sequoia-base:latest`, or a local VM's name. Tart must have it before the run: `reeval image build` (or `tart pull`) pulls it, and `reeval run` refuses one `tart list` doesn't show.

maxConcurrent.description: The most Tart VMs at once, across the run: 1 or 2, and 2 when unset, since macOS runs at most two macOS VMs at a time.

memory.description: Memory each clone gets: `'8g'`, `'4096m'`, or bytes; the image's when unset.

ssh.description: Reach the VM over SSH when its Tart Guest Agent doesn't answer `tart exec`: as `user` (`admin` when unset), with `key`, a private key the image trusts, absolute or relative to the file it's written in.

TimeSplit.description: Where a turn's time went, in ms, summing to its `durationMs`. Each moment counts once, as the first of: `waitingMs`, a background job the agent waited on (from the call that started it through the polls that checked on it), `toolMs`, a tool call, `modelMs`, a model call, and `otherMs`, the rest (the harness's own work, and time between calls). `modelMs` is null when the turn's model calls weren't seen one by one: on a sandbox without the egress gateway, and on Cursor, whose turn is one stream; that time is in `otherMs`. Which calls wait is a heuristic over the transcript: a shell call run in the background (`run_in_background`, a trailing `&`, `nohup`, or the command a Cursor terminal file names), then `sleep` and `wait` commands, output tools (`BashOutput`, `TaskOutput`) and reads of a Cursor terminal file.

TokenUsage.description: The tokens one turn used, as its harness reported them. `input` excludes cache reads and writes (so the prompt was `input + cacheRead + cacheWrite`); `reasoning` is part of `output`.

UpstreamCount.description: An upstream provider behind a gateway, and how many of the attempt's calls it served.

VmImage.description: The image a `tart()` attempt's VM was cloned from.

digest.description: The OCI manifest digest (`sha256:…`) Tart had for it; null for a local VM, which has none.

ref.description: The image as `tart({ image })` names it.

WebEventType.description: The transcript events a harness may be unable to report.
